text: If you've been enjoying that partly cloudy midday lull, take one more look at the sky before it gets busy: this afternoon's the main event, with showers and a few embedded thunderstorms likely as a front works through, and the timing to watch is roughly 2 to 8 tonight. A couple of those storms could get on the stronger side, so if you're out and about, keep an eye up and have a place to duck inside. The high should land right around 80, with the muggy south wind gusting near 25 at times. The forecast models are split hard on just how wet it gets, from a quick 40% chance to a much soggier call, so I'd plan for real rain rather than a stray sprinkle. Things quiet down after 8 tonight, with just a slight leftover chance before it clears out. The lake's under a wind advisory with waves building to 2 to 4 feet, so if you're out on the water, be in by early evening. Friday looks calmer and cooler, near 78 with just a morning shower chance.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Thursday! Today is a First Alert Weather Day due to the risk of strong to severe thunderstorms this afternoon and evening. The Storm Prediction Center has placed most of the region under a Marginal Risk (Level 1 of 5) for severe weather, but southwestern Vermont including portions of Addison, Rutland and Bennington counties have been upgraded to a Slight Risk (Level 2 of 5) for severe weather. Our day starts partly sunny and building humidity this morning will push temperatures into the mid-80s, boosting atmospheric energy ahead of an approaching cold front. Thunderstorms are expected to develop across northern New York by mid-afternoon and move eastward into Vermont between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m. The main window we will watch is between about 2 p.m. and 8 p.m.
